headline: High: Khoj can read shared notes/files while Authelia has broad network egress, creating default-path leakage and trust-boundary risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and uses RAG plus optional web search, so attacker-controlled content in shared notes can influence its outputs. Authelia can consume OAuth/ForwardAuth flows and has broad network egress, but no direct parser bridge is documented. The interaction is inferred from docs, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF attacker-controlled text is added to notes indexed by Khoj, THEN Khoj may surface it in responses.
IF Authelia consumes downstream content from Khoj without provenance checks, THEN prompt-like instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Restrict Khoj indexing to trusted folders only.
Add provenance labels to retrieved snippets.
Disable web search for untrusted corpora.
Review Authelia-facing content before forwarding.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping in the retrieval pipeline.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Authelia has broad network egress and handles OAuth/OIDC and ForwardAuth. If Authelia is placed in front of or adjacent to Khoj, sensitive note content can be exposed through networked flows or logs. The pairwise path is not directly evidenced, so I choose high because the default blast radius includes sensitive data and the safer interpretation is to escalate.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes personal notes containing sensitive data, THEN those data are in scope.
IF Authelia forwards or logs request context tied to Khoj access, THEN sensitive metadata may leak outward.
mitigations: Limit Khoj to non-sensitive collections.
Turn off verbose request logging in the Authelia path.
Separate credentials for Authelia and Khoj.
Review outbound destinations for both services.
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention controls on forwarded headers and logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia cannot write files or modify git state, and Khoj also lacks filesystem write and git modification capabilities. Both have broad network egress, but the rubric’s write-conflict indicators are absent. This makes direct capability conflict unlikely and the remaining overlap is limited to read/network use.
conditions: IF both agents are granted the same mutable external API scope, THEN conflicts could arise there.
IF an operator adds a shared writable directory, THEN conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep separate service accounts.
Avoid shared writable mounts.
Document ownership of any shared API.
Monitor for duplicate outbound actions.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat system that can present indexed content as answers, and Authelia can act on authentication/authorization flows via OIDC or ForwardAuth. If Authelia or an operator treats Khoj output as authoritative, errors can cascade into access decisions. No verification step is documented in the pair, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Khoj-generated text is used to justify access decisions, THEN incorrect retrieval can cascade.
IF Authelia consumes Khoj output without human verification, THEN downstream auth actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review for auth-related decisions.
Mark Khoj output as advisory only.
Log source snippets alongside answers.
Add a verification checklist before acting.
requires-engineering: enforce policy checks before any auth decision uses retrieved text.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly stores personal notes and indexed documents, while Authelia is an authentication layer with broad network egress. If personal or EU-origin data flow through Authelia into Khoj’s indexed store or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU personal data is indexed by Khoj through Authelia-mediated access, THEN residency/retention review is required.
IF Authelia logs identifiers tied to Khoj content, THEN subject-rights handling may diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before indexing.
Minimize auth logs.
Set retention limits on both systems.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and deletion propagation.
